subtitle_zh: On-policy distillation becomes the second pillar of post-training
headline_zh: In 2027, LLM post-training moved from a single GRPO recipe to a hybrid of RLVR and on-policy distillation (OPD). OPD papers grew from 1 to 907, while the GRPO family's share held flat. Qwen3/Qwen3.5 became the default base models. On the architecture side, looped recurrence, Gated DeltaNet hybrid attention, Muon and FP4 training are rising.

stats.note_zh: 1 paper → 907 papers; the fastest growth in this area

insights.body_zh: On-policy distillation (OPD) went from 0.1% → 20.5% of post-training methods, while the GRPO family went 39.3% → 38.2%. In OPD, a teacher scores the student token by token on the student's own sampled trajectories. This replaces RLVR's sparse outcome reward with a dense signal. OPD has not replaced RL: 36.5% of the 907 OPD papers also use GRPO/RLVR. What it pushed out was DPO and classic RLHF.
insights.note_zh: Post-training method pool = papers mentioning any of GRPO/RLVR/OPD/DPO/RLHF/rubric/SFT. OPD scores with per-token (reverse) KL and needs no reward model. OPD/OPSD mention rate: 210.9 per 10k. Of the 907 papers, 34.8% still evaluate on math/AIME. DPO 95.9 → 57.2 per 10k; RLHF plus reward models 94.4 → 27.4 per 10k. The standard 2026 recipe was an SFT/distillation cold start plus GRPO/DAPO outcome rewards.

evidence.title: Gains and Collapse in On-Policy Distillation: A Reinforcement Learning Perspective
When Teachers Conflict with Verifiers: Support-Preserving On-Policy Distillation
From Imitation to Reward Discovery: On-Policy Warmup for Agentic RL
The Art of Scaling Reinforcement Learning Compute for LLMs

insights.body_zh: 42% of OPD papers use on-policy self-distillation (OPSD). The teacher is the student itself, given a reference solution or execution feedback in the prompt. Within a year this line turned to patching: 24.1% of papers address collapse and instability, 9.3% use multiple teachers, and 2.1% do cross-tokenizer distillation. The trend holds excluding formulaic papers, but acceptance prospects for incremental work are uncertain.
insights.note_zh: Privileged information mentions 6.1 → 60.2 per 10k. OPSD gives per-token correction directions for failed trajectories in RLVR groups where every sample is wrong. Spillover: multimodal work is 24.6%, agentic OPD went 0 → 37.2 per 10k, and OPD also reaches block diffusion language models. OPD had no accepted precedent in 2026. About 52–53% of submissions in the OPD and OPSD clusters are flagged as formulaic writing; excluding them, the OPD mention rate is still 181.9 per 10k.

evidence.title: ImmuneCoT: Learning Reasoning Immunity via Privileged On-Policy Self-Distillation
On-Policy Self-Distillation without Any Supervision

insights.title_zh: GRPO research turns to training–inference consistency
insights.body_zh: Among GRPO/RLVR papers, entropy and exploration fell 24.5% → 14.5%, multi-turn/agent rose 19.1% → 31.1%, and credit assignment rose 3.7% → 14.7%. No named successor algorithm became the new standard; DAPO went 18.2 → 17.2 per 10k. New growth comes from engineering problems. Training–inference mismatch rose 4.5 → 12.8 per 10k, and RL stability under native NVFP4 precision has started to appear.
insights.note_zh: Sample: papers mentioning GRPO/RLVR, 727 in 2026 and 1,694 in 2027. Other topic shares: length/efficiency 39.1% → 27.5%, theoretical analysis 14.0% → 7.6%, using failures/negative samples 8.5% → 14.8%, hints/privileged guidance 6.1% → 12.8%. Mention rates (per 10k): GSPO 5.6 → 6.5, Dr.GRPO 2.5 → 2.1, entropy collapse 13.1 → 7.0. Training–inference mismatch covers mismatch between the rollout engine and the training engine, and trust regions that break after quantization.

evidence.title: Quantization Breaks Trust Region: Repairing Clipped RL Objective under Training--Inference Mismatch
TRIAGE: Direction-Aware Mismatch Stabilization for Native NVFP4 Reinforcement Learning
Bounding Token Divergence to Unlock Stable Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Models
TROLL: Trust Regions Improve Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Models

insights.title_zh: Credit assignment becomes the hottest RL subproblem
insights.body_zh: The main RL setting moved from single-turn math to long-horizon agents. Papers with credit assignment in the title or keywords went 9.1 → 102.8 per 10k. Benchmarks moved with it, from AIME (1.30% → 0.56%) to SWE-bench (0.19% → 0.63%). In 2026, GRPO papers on credit assignment had an acceptance rate of 0.59, against about 0.33 for GRPO overall.
insights.note_zh: Credit assignment matches turn-level/step-level credit or credit assignment in the title/keywords. Cluster 111 (Credit assignment for agentic RL) 12.1 → 86.5 per 10k. Agentic/multi-turn RL 29.3 → 75.6 per 10k; environment synthesis/scaling 6.1 → 19.8; RL in SWE/terminal settings 28.8 → 43.2. AIME and SWE-bench figures are shares of all submissions. The credit assignment acceptance-rate sample is n=27.

insights.title_zh: Rubric rewards begin to replace preference reward models
insights.body_zh: Rubric mentions went 38.9 → 118.1 per 10k, and the rubric share of post-training methods 4.2% → 11.5%. Classic RLHF fell 94.4 → 27.4 over the same period. The 2027 focus is automatic rubric generation, co-evolution with the policy, and defenses against reward hacking. Reviewers accept rubric-based evaluation but remain cautious about rubric-RL methods: in 2026, rubric papers had an acceptance rate of 0.364, the rubric-reward cluster only 0.235.
insights.note_zh: Title/keyword basis: 11.6 → 41.8 per 10k. Generative reward models (GenRM) 11.1 → 2.3 per 10k; the RLHF and reward modeling cluster 44.4 → 13.3. The rubric-reward cluster's full name is Rubric rewards and reward hacking. Accepted rubric work in 2026 was mostly evaluation benchmarks (ProfBench, ExpertLongBench and others); few method papers used rubrics as RL rewards. 2027 also brings rubric-level credit assignment; defenses include precision objectives and reliability triage.

evidence.title: Co-Evolving Policy and Rubric via Capability Awareness for Open-Ended Generation
Eat Your Precision: Precision Objective Mitigates Reward Hacking in Rubric-based RL
Dr.Credit: Rubric-Grounded Process Credit Assignment for Deep Research Agents
Chasing the Tail: Effective Rubric-based Reward Modeling for Large Language Model Post-Training

insights.title_zh: R1-era reasoning and overthinking topics cool
insights.body_zh: DeepSeek-R1 mentions fell 83.8 → 17.2 per 10k, overthinking 43.4 → 9.8, and math reasoning 95.4 → 26.7. Efficient reasoning held its share, but the question moved from compressing CoT length to when to stop and per-token adaptive compute. Latent reasoning rose 45.9 → 75.1 per 10k and is starting to merge with looped architectures.
insights.note_zh: Math reasoning is the LLM mathematical reasoning cluster. Efficient-reasoning concept share 1.20% → 1.18%. Chain-of-thought and latent reasoning cluster 87.3 → 40.5 per 10k; test-time scaling 165.5 → 130.0. The 2026 overthinking cluster had an acceptance rate of 0.252. The winners were a few papers with clear mechanisms, such as the oral on decoupled rewards plus curriculum scheduling. Representative adaptive-compute work: PonderLM-3.

insights.title_zh: Qwen3 becomes the default base for post-training research
insights.body_zh: From 2025 → 2027, the share of LLM papers mentioning Qwen went 2.2% → 9.7% → 21.1%, and Llama 14.5% → 8.7% → 6.6%. The two crossed in 2026. Among 2027 RL/OPD papers, Qwen appears in 31.4% and Llama in 3.0%. Llama-3.1-8B mentions are still rising, but mostly as a generic baseline in safety and interpretability work.
insights.note_zh: Shares are within the two LLM themes. Model mention rates (per 10k): Qwen3-8B 21.2 → 108.6, Qwen3-4B 14.6 → 76.5, Qwen3-30B-A3B (MoE testbed) 6.6 → 17.9, Qwen3.5 0 → 122.3; Qwen3-VL 0.5 → 75.1, overtaking Qwen2.5-VL (56.5 → 48.8). Llama-3.1-8B: 69.0 per 10k across all submissions. DeepSeek-R1-Distill 21.7 → 14.6, OLMo 41.9 → 63.7 (fully open data helps contamination and attribution studies), Kimi 8.6 → 23.7, GLM-4.5+ 5.0 → 26.3, gpt-oss flat at 17.2. In 2026, within the LLM themes, papers using Qwen3 had an acceptance rate of 0.352, those using Llama 0.275.

evidence.title: Counterfactual Visual On-Policy Distillation
Protect What Is at Risk, Distill Where It Responds: On-Policy Distillation for Continual Learning in MLLMs

insights.title_zh: Looped recurrence and hybrid linear attention rise
insights.body_zh: Looped Transformers (looped / recurrent-depth) are the fastest-growing architecture direction, 10.1 → 50.9 per 10k, with a 2026 acceptance rate of 0.50. Gated DeltaNet (GDN) went 2.0 → 18.8 per 10k and Mamba 70.7 → 53.5. Pure SSMs are giving way to hybrids of GDN plus a few full-attention layers. Supporting work followed, including KV eviction for hybrid models, recurrent-state compression and DSA-style sparse attention.
insights.note_zh: Papers naming Ouro/Huginn: 1.0 → 7.9 per 10k. 2027 looped topics include training recipes, stabilization, FlashLoop-style acceleration and length extrapolation; 2026 mean rating 4.82. DeltaNet 2.5 → 23.2 per 10k; Linear attention & DeltaNet hybrids cluster 17.7 → 26.7; SSM cluster 25.2 → 15.3. The hybrid design follows the Qwen3-Next/Qwen3.5 line. DSA-style indexer plus top-k sparse attention 0 → 7.0 per 10k. Other work covers transferring recurrent states across models and MTP parallel verification on hybrid models.

evidence.title: Closing the Loop: Practical Training Recipes for Looped Language Models
Simply Stabilizing the Loop via Fully Looped Transformer
Rotary-state Gated DeltaNet: Enhancing State Tracking through Rotation
HybriKV: KV Cache Eviction for Hybrid Linear-Attention Language Models

insights.title_zh: Efficiency research follows reasoning and agent workloads
insights.body_zh: KV cache research went 1.03% → 1.83%, driven by long-reasoning decoding and multi-turn agent settings. On the training side, Muon went 24.2 → 51.4 per 10k and is starting to be used for RL and fine-tuning; FP4 training went 6.6 → 16.5. Structured pruning and LoRA are receding, with 2026 acceptance rates of only 0.198 and 0.192, the lowest in the area.
insights.note_zh: KV breakdown (per 10k): long-reasoning decoding 16.7 → 29.3, multi-turn/agent 7.6 → 21.9, prefix/KV reuse 5.0 → 25.3, KV quantization 3.5 → 12.6. Muon in 2026: acceptance rate 0.354, mean rating 4.76; Polar Express got an oral. FP4 means NVFP4/MXFP4, 2026 acceptance rate 0.538. Pruning and LoRA are counted by cluster: structured pruning 63.6 → 28.1 per 10k, LoRA 63.1 → 47.2. Scaling law mentions 87.3 → 60.9. Speculative decoding cluster 35.8 → 53.2, EAGLE 12.6 → 8.4; novelty comes from action-level speculation for agents and verification on hybrid models.

rewarded_2026_zh: In 2026 the two LLM themes had 3,749 submissions and an acceptance rate of 0.286, slightly above the 0.27 baseline for all submissions. Work with clear, scalable mechanisms was rewarded: long-context training and evaluation 0.479, diffusion language models 0.472, pretraining data 0.387. Incremental compression and formulaic methods did poorly: LoRA/PEFT cluster 0.192, structured pruning 0.198, joint compression and quantization 0.171.
frontline_zh: The standard OPSD form: after seeing a reference solution or execution feedback, the model acts as its own teacher. This fixes the missing gradient in all-wrong RLVR groups.
Division of labor between OPD and RL: OPD first as an on-policy warmup, then agentic RL.
Cross-tokenizer OPD lets Qwen3 students learn from teachers of other model families; multi-teacher setups are 9.3% of OPD papers.
OPD extends to block diffusion LMs, video generation and full-duplex spoken dialogue.
RL infrastructure becomes a paper topic, e.g. training–inference mismatch from quantized rollouts and NVFP4 RL stabilization.
Inference systems adapt to hybrid architectures: fused kernels for DSA indexers, KV eviction and state compression for hybrid models.
watchlist_zh: Whether OPD gets through review. It had no accepted precedent in 2026; work that analyzes collapse and distillability is more likely to win.
Whether RLVR and OPD unify into one objective, and whether OPD works for continual learning and against forgetting.
Whether looped models reach real pretraining and merge with latent reasoning and test-time scaling.
As GDN hybrids spread, KV, speculative decoding and quantization research shifts its target to recurrent states and indexers.
Low-precision RL and training–inference mismatch may replace entropy collapse as the main RL stability thread in 2027.
notes_zh: "Per 10k" is the number of papers per 10k submissions that match the term or cluster; a share is the proportion within the relevant paper pool or theme.
OPD counts: the OPD cluster went 0.5 → 108.3 per 10k and the OPSD cluster 0 → 52.3, the two fastest-growing clusters in this area. OPD/OPSD combined is about 211 per 10k.
The post-training method pool has 1,851 papers in 2026 and 4,432 in 2027. RLHF/reward-model share 27.9% → 14.2%; GRPO family 39.3% → 38.2%.
GRPO/RLVR family 366.9 → 393.8 per 10k, i.e. +7%. Among RL/OPD papers, Qwen:Llama≈10:1.
Looped cluster 7.1 → 34.9 per 10k. The direction's 2026 acceptance rate was 0.50 (n=20, mean rating 4.82), against a 0.27 baseline.
Qwen3-family mentions are counted across all submissions; Qwen3.5 separately went 0 → 122.3 per 10k. In the rising/falling lists, OPD is 1 paper in 2026 → 907 papers in 2027.

2026 acceptance-rate details: llm_post 0.292, llm_core 0.279. High payoff: the two RLVR reasoning clusters 0.415 and 0.382, SFT↔RL relationship 0.385, Lean theorem proving 0.422, long-context training and evaluation mean rating 4.71, pretraining data mean rating 4.81 (highest in the area), scaling laws 0.388, sparse attention 0.391, SSM 0.38. At the concept level: diffusion language models mean rating 4.67, looped 0.385 (mean rating 4.92), Muon 0.377 (mean rating 4.74).

Acceptance rates within GRPO papers: credit assignment 0.59 (n=27), off-policy/replay 0.47, pass@k 0.46, Qwen2.5-based papers only 0.26. Other low-payoff directions: multi-hop RAG 0.196, prompt optimization 0.216, MoE architectures 0.22, KV compression 0.232, rubric/reward hacking 0.235, overthinking 0.252.
The 51 orals in 2026 include The Art of Scaling RL Compute, Coverage Principle, Mamba-3, Polar Express (Muon), TROLL, OpenThoughts, ThinKV, MemAgent, LoongRL and others.

Representative frontier work. OPSD: ImmuneCoT, SE-OPSD, Posterior Teachers. OPD–RL division of labor: On-Policy Warmup, VALVE (critic-guided OPD), PivotOPD (multi-turn agents recovering from critical errors), plus work on preserving support when teacher and verifier conflict. Cross-tokenizer: byte-prefix marginalization, Breaking the Tokenizer Barrier. Non-text OPD: unbiased OPD for block diffusion, StepX-OPD. RL infrastructure: Quantization Breaks Trust Region, TRIAGE, miniTE.

More frontier work: train-inference mismatch 4.5 → 12.8 per 10k. Environment supply for agent RL includes recursive environment evolution, replayable environments and terminal environment families (SCOPE, Terminal-Universe); environment synthesis 6.1 → 19.8, SWE/terminal RL 28.8 → 43.2. DSA implementations include LiteTopK, LISA and DoSA; indexer papers went from 0 to 30. Inference systems for hybrid architectures include HybriKV, DASC, Xtra-MTP and LatentPort. Muon moves beyond pretraining: When Does Muon Help Agentic RL, and optimizer mismatch in Muon fine-tuning. The quantizability of MLA caches depends on the training recipe (When Cleaner Caches Break).

Testbeds: Qwen3-8B/Qwen3-4B are the default post-training scales, Qwen3-30B-A3B is the MoE testbed, and Qwen3.5 reached 122.3 per 10k on first appearance. Evaluation is moving from AIME (1.30% → 0.56%)/MATH-500 to SWE-bench (0.19% → 0.63%), τ-bench and OSWorld.

Watch-list additions: about half of the 907 OPD submissions in 2027 use formulaic writing. A representative continual-learning paper is On-Policy Distillation for Continual Learning in MLLMs. For looped models in real pretraining, see Ouro. Low-precision RL means NVFP4.
